post.caption: A stuck carriage cost Napoleon a brooch. In 1815, his carriage got stuck in mud after Waterloo, and he left it and everything in it behind. It held medals and a jewelry box of loose diamonds. One piece was a diamond brooch made around 1810, most likely a hat ornament for special occasions. Nearly 100 old mine cut diamonds surround its center stone. Three days after the battle, it was offered to Prussia's king, and it stayed with the House of Hohenzollern for generations. Sotheby's sold it in Geneva on November 12, 2025. Its center diamond weighs 13.04 carats.
